newsitem.title: USA: Texas sowing, harvesting advance with mild weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas sowing, harvesting advance with mild weather.

text.p: Mild weather allowed fieldwork in Texas to advance during the week ended Sunday, the weekly state crop report said.
Small grains seeding continued in many areas of the state while harvest operation on cotton and sorghum also progressed.
Armyworm activity slowed because of the cooler nights, but spraying continued on some pastures. The report said damage was already "severe" in some areas.
Wheat planted 85 percent vs 74 week ago, 58 year ago, 66 on a five-year average.
Wheat emerged 69 pct vs 51 w/a, 36 y/a, 44 avg.
Corn harvested 91 pct vs 84 w/a, 88 y/a, 91 avg.
Corn mature 100 pct vs 98 w/a, 100 y/a, 99 avg.
Corn rated 92 percent good/excellent vs 92 w/a.
Sorghum harvested 68 pct vs 65 w/a, 83 y/a, 79 avg.
Sorghum mature 94 pct vs 88 w/a, 93 y/a, 89 avg.
Sorghum rated 65 pct good/excellent vs 54 w/a.
Cotton bolls opening 75 pct vs 66 w/a, 66 y/a, 67 avg.
Cotton harvested 21 pct vs 19 w/a, 32 y/a, 32 avg.
Cotton rated 49 pct good/excellent vs 44 w/a.
Pasture and range condition was rated 52 pct good to excellent, versus 49 percent at that level last week.
